text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Head of OSCE mission Gonzales will make public his report on local elections in Serbia on December 27, in which he will request annulment of election fraud and broader democratisation, says a Western diplomat in Belgrade.
- Supreme Court of Serbia accepts Zajedno appeal for extraordinary review of municipal court decision to annul its victory in Nis.
- OSCE delegation does not have the right to make conclusions, it can only express its opinion, says Serbian Prime Minister Marjanovic in interview.
- Montenegrin Parliament accept Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic's program and ministers.
- Banja Luka court began trial against Bosnian Presidency President Alija Izetbegovic for war crimes.
- Kosovo Albanians open diplomatic mission in Istanbul, says Pristina daily Bujku.
- Eurofima approved Yugoslav railways a 10 million swiss franc credit for the reconstruction and purchase of new trains, says Yugoslav Railways' CEO Zivorad Maksimovic.
- Federal Parliament's Chamber of Republics and Chamber of Citizens to hold sessions Thursday and Friday to pass 1997 budget.
- UNTAES prevented the fight which broke out in Ilok between Croatians going to church and carrying Croatian symbols and local Serbs from acquiring greater proportions.
- Bosnian Serb General Manojlovic transfers duties to Bosnian Serb General Staff commander Pero Colic.
- Serbian Private Entrepreneurship Minister Djukic confirmed he would resign in the next few days because of "constitutional violations".
